html:
The Battle of the Indus was fought on 24 November 1221 on the bank of the Indus River, in the north of today's Pakistan. Genghis Khan destroyed the last army of the Khwarazmian Empire, led by the prince Jalal al-Din.

The Mongols had invaded Khwarazm in 1219 and taken its great cities. The shah fled and died. His son Jalal al-Din fought on. He raised an army at Ghazni in Afghanistan and beat a Mongol force at Parwan, the only serious Mongol defeat of the war. Genghis Khan came after him in person. Jalal al-Din's allies quarrelled over the spoils and left him, and he fell back east. The Mongols caught him as he was about to cross the Indus. He put his back to the river and held for some hours, until a Mongol force crossed a ridge thought impassable and hit his flank. With his army lost, he rode his horse off a high bank into the river and swam across.

The battle ended the conquest of Khwarazm. Jalal al-Din found refuge for a time near the Delhi Sultanate. The Mongols raided the Punjab but did not stay, and Genghis Khan turned for home.
